title: THE GREAT ECONOMIC ILLUSION: Where are we heading and where does AI fit it?
description: Send us Fan Mail Preparing for AI is back with the first epsiode of Series 3! The gap between the ultra-wealthy and everyone else isn't just growing—it's accelerating at an alarming rate and we need to talk about it. In this thought-provoking episode, we tackle the uncomfortable truth that wealth inequality underpins virtually every major social problem we're facing today. Drawing inspiration from economist Gary Stevenson's work, we explore how our obsession with GDP growth has created an economic illusion that ignores human wellbeing and environmental sustainability. The "trickle-down" promise has proven hollow, with wealth consistently moving upward rather than downward. Meanwhile, property and assets become increasingly concentrated among a tiny percentage of the population, leaving younger generations with diminishing prospects. But what happens when we add AI to this already precarious equation? Technology has historically enabled continued growth by finding more efficient ways to use resources, but AI represents something fundamentally different. It threatens to make large portions of the workforce economically irrelevant, potentially creating what we describe as "techno-feudalism" – a society where a tiny elite owns everything while most humans subsist on universal basic income. Yet AI might also be our salvation. Sufficiently advanced systems could help design economic frameworks that balance human needs with planetary boundaries, similar to Kate Raworth's "Donut Economics" model. The challenge lies in convincing those with power to implement changes that benefit everyone, not just themselves. Have we reached a breaking point where our economic system must evolve or collapse? And what would you personally be willing to give up for a more equitable society? Join the conversation and share your thoughts in the comments.
summary: The season three opener, inspired by Gary's Economics, argues that wealth inequality underpins nearly every societal problem: trickle-down was a lie, the UK middle class is being hollowed out toward '0.5% and peasants', and land and property lock wealth into an untaxed hereditary elite. AI is cast as both accelerator - toward trillionaire techno-feudalism and 'useless eaters' - and potential savior: Jimmy deep-researched a 'Balanced Prosperity Model' (net wealth tax above 500k, sovereign wealth fund, universal basic services, carbon dividends) live on air, while both hosts conclude the answers already exist and the unsolved problem is that the powerful will never accept them, pointing instead to social unrest and revolution.
keyTalkingPoints: The great economic illusion: 40+ years of GDP-growth obsession and the neoliberal trickle-down promise delivered wealth concentration instead - 'it's trickle-up economics' - with exponential growth on a finite planet compared to cancer cells

Gary's Economics: government and personal debt is owned by the wealthy, and a net wealth tax (Norway-style, with pension and primary-home allowances) is the fix; the 'they'll all leave' objection is rebutted by non-resident landlord taxes on UK property

UK wealth is locked in land: most land is owned by a tiny number of families (the royals included), the triple-lock protects an asset-rich older generation, and younger generations hold nothing as prices outrun wages

AI as disruptor: automation could take half of jobs within 5-20 years, destroying purchasing power and crashing demand economies - or fund a UBI utopia; on the current system it accelerates toward neo-feudalism where most humans are 'economically irrelevant'

AI as savior: it could replace think tanks and design palatable policy; Jimmy's o3-high deep research produced a 15-year 'Balanced Prosperity Model' for the UK - but Matt notes it merely rehashes ideas think tanks already had

The catch: the answers already exist (donut economics, wealth taxes, UBS) - the unsolved problem is that people with real power stand to lose, so both hosts land on social collapse and revolution rather than prophylactic reform; both would give up consumer choice and flights for a fairer society

He would give up frequent flying, gadgets and consumer choice for a more equal society
matt: The fiat currency system is a doomed pyramid scheme and capitalism is doomed partly because of AI - he has hedged with physical gold (up ~25%)
Donut economics and ecological economics point the way: a mature economy should pursue qualitative improvement within planetary boundaries, like a mature forest, not infinite quantitative growth
The barrier to reform is human nature: those with power and money will not accept loss, so collapse or revolution is the default path unless AI can sell them a win-win
It is not hopeless - who we elect and what power we allow still matters - but we must stop pretending the answers haven't already been thought of
